module_title: The World Bank Group (WBG) and Advanced Mechanisms
introduction: The 'World Bank Group' is a family of five international organizations. This advanced level explores the roles of the remaining three branches and the concept of 'IMF Conditionality'.

core_concepts.title: The 5 Branches of World Bank Group
core_concepts.description:
Besides IBRD and IDA, the WBG includes: 
3. IFC (International Finance Corporation): Focuses on the 'Private Sector' in developing countries. 
4. MIGA (Multilateral Investment Guarantee Agency): Provides 'Political Risk Insurance' to foreign investors. 
5. ICSID (International Centre for Settlement of Investment Disputes): Settles disputes between foreign investors and governments.

core_concepts.title: India and ICSID
core_concepts.description: This is a critical exam point: India is a member of the first four branches (IBRD, IDA, IFC, MIGA) but is NOT a member of 'ICSID'. India believes ICSID's rules are biased toward developed nations.

core_concepts.title: IMF Conditionality (Bailouts)
core_concepts.description: When the IMF provides a 'Bailout' (like it did for India in 1991), it imposes strict 'Conditions'. These usually involve cutting government spending (Austerity), removing subsidies, devaluing currency, and opening up the economy (Liberalization). This is often called the 'Washington Consensus'.

important_entities.name: The Washington Consensus
important_entities.significance: Coined in 1989, it refers to a set of 10 economic policy prescriptions (like privatization and deregulation) that the IMF and World Bank typically require from countries in crisis.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.alert_title: World Bank vs. World Bank Group
trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Be careful with wording: 'World Bank' = IBRD + IDA. 'World Bank Group (WBG)' = All 5 institutions combined.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: MIGA is the insurance arm of the World Bank Group.

exam_strategy_tips: Question: 'Which organization of the WBG lends to the private sector?' Answer: IFC. This is a very common UPSC/State PCS question.
